detail.purpose: Lets a visitor pick one of the five roles (Donor, NGO, Volunteer / NGO Transporter, Admin, CSR Sponsor) and sign in straight away with that role's instant synthetic demo account. It is the front door of the pilot.

layout.contents: Product name 'Anna Mitra' and a one-line description: lets restaurants post surplus edible food, matches it to nearby NGOs, coordinates volunteer pickup and reports confirmed rescue impact.
Five role cards or buttons: Donor, NGO, Volunteer / NGO Transporter, Admin, CSR Sponsor. Each shows the role name and one short line describing what that role does.
After a role is picked, a short panel shows the synthetic demo account for that role and a 'Enter demo' button. Note that all people and details are synthetic.
Links to 'Log in with my account' (/login) and 'Create an account' (/signup).

shows.details: Five roles in this order: Donor, NGO, Volunteer / NGO Transporter, Admin, CSR Sponsor. No counts or totals.
Synthetic account for the chosen role, shown so the visitor knows which account they are entering.

actions.action: Picks the Donor role and selects 'Enter demo'.
actions.result: Signed in to the demo Donor account and sent to /donor-dashboard.

actions.action: Picks the NGO role and selects 'Enter demo'.
actions.result: Signed in to the demo NGO account and sent to /ngo-feed.

actions.action: Picks the volunteer role and selects 'Enter demo'.
actions.result: Signed in to the demo volunteer account and sent to /volunteer-tasks.

actions.action: Picks the Admin role and selects 'Enter demo'.
actions.result: Signed in to the demo admin account and sent to /admin-operations.

actions.action: Picks the CSR Sponsor role and selects 'Enter demo'.
actions.result: Signed in to the demo sponsor account and sent to /sponsor-impact.

actions.action: Chooses 'Log in with my account' or 'Create an account' instead of a demo.
actions.result: Goes to /login or /signup.

links.label: Enter demo (Donor)
links.when: After the Donor role is picked and demo sign-in succeeds.

links.label: Enter demo (NGO)
links.when: After the NGO role is picked and demo sign-in succeeds.

links.label: Enter demo (Volunteer / NGO Transporter)
links.when: After the volunteer role is picked and demo sign-in succeeds.

links.label: Enter demo (Admin)
links.when: After the Admin role is picked and demo sign-in succeeds.

links.label: Enter demo (CSR Sponsor)
links.when: After the CSR Sponsor role is picked and demo sign-in succeeds.

links.label: Log in with my account

links.label: Create an account

states.empty: No role picked yet: the demo panel is hidden and only the five role choices and account links show.
states.loading: While the demo account signs in, the chosen role button shows a short busy indicator and is disabled.
states.error: If demo sign-in fails, a short message says the demo could not start and offers 'Log in with my account' instead.

detail.notes: Demo accounts are instant and synthetic; no real person, contact detail, address or coordinate is involved. Demo sign-in is for the hackathon pilot only. No OTP or KYC step is shown. Only role choice and demo entry happen here; no location is requested.

detail.purpose: Lets a donor, NGO, volunteer / NGO transporter or CSR sponsor create their own account. The account waits for admin approval before the person can use the app.

layout.contents: Heading 'Create your Anna Mitra account'. A line saying the account will be reviewed by an admin before it can be used.
Choice of who is signing up: Donor (restaurant staff), NGO (charity or food-relief organisation), Volunteer / NGO Transporter, or CSR Sponsor.
Fields for name, email and password, and a 'Create account' button. The exact extra fields for each account type are not specified in the requirements.
Text 'Already have an account? Log in' with a link to Login.

shows.details: Four options, one per persona: Donor, NGO, Volunteer / NGO Transporter, CSR Sponsor.
Text saying the account waits for admin approval before sign-in works.

actions.action: Creates a restaurant account by choosing Donor and filling in the form.
actions.result: Account is saved as pending admin approval. The person is told it is awaiting approval.

actions.action: Creates an organisation account by choosing NGO and filling in the form.
actions.result: Account is saved as pending admin approval. The person is told it is awaiting approval.

actions.action: Creates a volunteer account by choosing Volunteer / NGO Transporter and filling in the form.
actions.result: Account is saved as pending admin approval. The person is told it is awaiting approval.

actions.action: Creates a sponsor account by choosing CSR Sponsor and filling in the form.
actions.result: Account is saved as pending admin approval. The person is told it is awaiting approval.

links.label: Log in
links.when: The person already has an account and wants to sign in.

states.empty: Blank form with the account type unselected and the create button ready.
states.loading: Create button is disabled with a progress indicator while the account is being saved.
states.error: Problem message beside the field at fault (for example missing name, invalid email or weak password), and the form keeps what was typed.

detail.notes: Accounts are created pending admin approval; admins approve or suspend them on Admin Operations. No production OTP or KYC verification step is shown. All names, emails and details are synthetic for the hackathon. Password rules and any further required fields are not specified in the requirements.

'Forgot password?' link and a 'Create an account' link for new participants.

detail.purpose: Where a participant asks for a password reset link by email. Donors, NGOs, volunteers, admins and CSR sponsors all use it when they cannot sign in.

layout.contents: Heading "Forgot password" with a short line saying a reset link will be emailed to the account's address.
One email field and a "Send reset link" button.
Appears after submitting. Says a reset link has been sent to the email if it belongs to an account, and tells the person to check their inbox.
A "Back to sign in" link below the form.

actions.action: Enters the account email and taps "Send reset link".
actions.result: A reset link is emailed to that address and the confirmation message appears. The person then follows the emailed link to the Reset Password screen.

links.label: Back to sign in
links.when: The person remembers their password or wants to return to sign in without resetting.

links.label: Reset link in the email
links.when: The person opens the emailed link to set a new password. This is opened from the email, not from this screen.

states.empty: Email field is blank and the send button is disabled until something is typed.
states.loading: Send button shows a pending state and the form cannot be submitted again until the request finishes.
states.error: If the request cannot be sent, a message says the reset link could not be sent and the person can try again.

detail.notes: The emailed link is the only route to Reset Password; the screen itself has no link to it. Email is synthetic for the hackathon. The notification service is used when configured; if it is not configured, the app must still provide an explicit working fallback for resetting a password, which the requirements do not describe. Production-grade OTP or KYC verification is out of scope.

detail.purpose: Lets a participant set a new password from the reset link in their email. Any signed-in-out participant (donor, NGO, volunteer or transporter, admin, or CSR sponsor) arrives here from that link.

layout.contents: Heading 'Set a new password' with a short line saying the password will be changed for this account.
'New password' field, 'Confirm new password' field, and a 'Save new password' button.
Text link 'Request a new reset link' for when the link has expired or does not work, and a 'Back to sign in' link.

actions.action: Enters a new password and the same password again, then selects 'Save new password'.
actions.result: The password is changed for the account named in the emailed link and the person is taken to /login to sign in with the new password.

actions.action: Selects 'Request a new reset link'.
actions.result: The person is taken to /forgot-password to ask for a fresh emailed link.

links.label: Back to sign in

links.label: Request a new reset link

states.loading: While the new password is being saved, the button is disabled and shows a saving indicator.

detail.notes: The emailed link is the only check; there is no OTP or KYC step. Password strength rules are not set in the requirements. The two password fields must match before saving. Permissions and the reset itself are enforced on the server.

detail.purpose: Lets any signed-in participant (donor, NGO, volunteer/transporter, admin or CSR sponsor) see their own account details, change their name, email or password, and sign out.

layout.contents: Heading 'Profile' with a one-line note that these details belong to the signed-in account.
Shows the current name and email, each with an Edit control. Shows the participant's role (Donor, NGO, Volunteer / NGO Transporter, Admin or CSR Sponsor) as read-only text.
Single 'Name' field pre-filled with the current name, and a 'Save name' button.
'New email' field and a 'Save email' button.
'Current password', 'New password' and 'Confirm new password' fields, and a 'Change password' button.
A 'Sign out' button at the bottom of the screen.

layout.contents: Heading with the restaurant's name and a primary button "Post surplus food"; a secondary control "Repeat last donation" for one-tap repeat posting.
Recent donations of this restaurant, newest first, each row showing the food description, portions, pickup-by time and current status; each row opens its donation detail.
Simple counts of this restaurant's donations by status (for example published, claimed, delivered), so the donor sees where things stand at a glance.
Links to restaurant preferences and to the full donation tracking list.

Number of this restaurant's donations in each status.

detail.purpose: Where a donor posts surplus edible food by voice, typing or manually, or repeats a past donation with one tap, then completes a fresh handling checklist and publishes it. Only donors use this screen.

layout.contents: Heading 'Quick Post' with a short line saying the donation is posted in under 60 seconds. A 'Cancel' link back to the donor dashboard.
A 'Repeat last donation' one-tap button that fills the food description, portions and pickup-by time from the restaurant's previous donation. Shown only when a previous donation exists.

A 'Speak' button and a text box for the food description, plus a 'Type manually' option when voice or AI is unavailable. Fields for number of portions and pickup-by time are beside or below the text box.

Editable fields for food description, portions and pickup-by time, pre-filled from the spoken or typed text. Each value can be edited before publishing. Shows a notice when AI extraction is unavailable and values must be entered by hand.

A fresh checklist with three sections: preparation time, storage and handling, and allergens. Each section has the fields the donor must answer; none are pre-ticked from earlier posts or from restaurant preferences.
An optional 'Add photo' control. A 'Publish donation' primary button at the bottom.

shows.details: Food description, portions and pickup-by time of the restaurant's last donation, used only to pre-fill the form.
Food description, number of portions and pickup-by time, in that order, each editable before publishing.
Preparation time, storage and handling, allergens. All blank at the start of each post.
Optional single photo preview once added.

Food description, portions still available, pickup-by time, and the donor restaurant name. Shows the match explanation the NGO saw in the feed.
Choice of 'Claim all' or 'Claim part', a portions field that appears for part claims and is limited to portions still available, and a 'Confirm claim' button.
Countdown showing time left to confirm the claim, starting at the reservation timeout (default 5 minutes). Shows a notice that unconfirmed portions are released when it runs out.
After confirming, shows the portions reserved for the NGO, the pickup-by time, and a button 'View donation' to the donation's details. Shows a clear message if the claim failed.

shows.details: Food description, portions available, pickup-by time, donor restaurant name, match explanation from the feed.
Live remaining count after other claims; portions reserved by others are not offered.
Countdown in minutes and seconds to the window close, default 5 minutes and configurable.
Portions reserved for this NGO and the pickup-by time, once confirmed.

actions.action: Chooses 'Claim all' or 'Claim part' and enters the portions to claim when claiming part.
actions.result: Form checks the quantity is at least 1 and no more than the portions still available.

actions.action: Confirms the claim before the window closes.
actions.result: The portions are reserved for this NGO and the claim result panel shows them. Portions cannot be over-allocated to two NGOs.

actions.action: Lets the confirmation window run out without confirming.
actions.result: The reservation is released and the portions return to the feed for other NGOs.

links.label: Back to feed
links.when: The NGO leaves without claiming, or after the window closes.

links.label: View donation
links.when: After a successful claim, to see the donation's details and status history.

states.empty: If no donation is selected or it is no longer available, shows 'This donation is no longer available' with a link back to the feed.
states.loading: Shows a skeleton of the donation summary and disables the claim button until the donation and remaining portions load.
states.error: If another NGO took the portions or the window has closed, shows the reason and the portions left, and offers 'Back to feed'.

detail.notes: Server-side enforcement of quantity limits, the claim deadline and the window; claims use transactions or equivalent concurrency controls so portions are never over-allocated. Only NGO accounts that are approved can claim. Reservation timeout is configurable, default 5 minutes. No live location is used. In-app alerts may prompt the NGO to return here but are delivered by the notification service only when configured.

/ngo-claim.basis: ["NGO Claim","Where an NGO claims all or part of a donation within the confirmation window.",["NGO"],[["NGO","claim all or part of a donation before the window closes"]]]

detail.purpose: Where an NGO confirms how many portions it actually received from a donation it claimed. Only NGO-confirmed quantities count as rescued food in the impact reporting.

layout.contents: Heading 'Confirm received quantity' with a short line saying the confirmed amount is what counts as rescued food.
Donation's food description, pickup-by time, donor restaurant name, and the portions the NGO claimed.
Number input for portions received, pre-filled with the claimed portions, plus an optional note field.
Button labelled 'Confirm received' with a line that confirmation is final.

shows.details: Food description, donor restaurant name, pickup-by time, claimed portions.
Editable portions number, defaulting to the claimed portions.

actions.action: Enter the portions received and confirm
actions.result: The received quantity is saved and the donation is marked confirmed as delivered, so it counts toward rescued food.

actions.action: Enter fewer portions than claimed
actions.result: The confirmed quantity is recorded as the lower figure; the rest is not counted as rescued.

links.label: View donation
links.when: After confirming, to see the donation's details and status history.

states.empty: No claimed donation awaiting receipt: a short message saying there is nothing to confirm, with no form.
states.loading: Claim details show a loading placeholder while fetching.
states.error: If saving fails, a message says the confirmation was not saved and the entered quantity stays on screen for retry.

detail.notes: Received quantity cannot exceed the portions the NGO claimed; the server enforces this. Only the NGO that claimed the donation may confirm it. Confirmed portions feed the CSR sponsor dashboard. Requirements do not say how the screen is reached for a specific claim.

/ngo-receipt.basis: ["NGO Receipt","Where an NGO confirms the quantity it received.",["NGO"],[["NGO","confirm the quantity received"]]]

detail.purpose: Where an NGO sets its current need, capacity and availability so the matching feed offers it suitable donations. NGO staff use it whenever their needs or intake capacity change.

layout.contents: Heading 'Capacity' with a line saying this sets what your NGO can take now, and a note that the feed uses these settings to match donations.
A single switch labelled 'Accepting donations now' with on/off state text.
Input for current need, in portions, with a short hint saying how many portions you can use now.
Input for capacity, in portions, with a short hint saying the most your NGO can receive in one go.
A 'Save' button and a 'Cancel' link; a line showing when capacity was last updated.

shows.details: Current need value in portions, shown as an editable field.
Capacity value in portions, shown as an editable field.
On/off state of accepting donations, with the time it was last changed.

actions.action: Change the availability switch on or off
actions.result: The NGO's availability is updated and it is shown as accepting or not accepting donations in the matching feed.

actions.action: Enter current need and capacity in portions and press Save
actions.result: The values are saved and the page shows a confirmation with the new last-updated time.

actions.action: Enter a value that breaks a quantity rule and press Save
actions.result: The save is refused and the page explains which field is not allowed, leaving the entered values in place.

links.label: View matching donations
links.when: After saving, to see which nearby donations now fit the updated need and capacity.

states.empty: No capacity saved yet: fields are blank with a prompt to enter current need and capacity before saving.
states.loading: Form shows placeholder fields while the saved capacity settings load.
states.error: A red message appears above the form if saving fails, and entered values stay on screen for retry.

detail.notes: Only an approved NGO can see and change its own capacity; the server enforces this and the quantity rules. Quantities are in portions. No live location is used; the NGO sets its availability manually. Changes apply to future matching and do not alter donations already claimed.

/ngo-capacity.basis: ["NGO Capacity","Where an NGO sets its current need, capacity and availability.",["NGO"],[["NGO","set current need, capacity and availability"]]]

detail.purpose: Where a volunteer or NGO transporter turns availability on or off, sets how much they can carry, and accepts a pickup to collect claimed food from a donor and hand it to the receiving NGO. Only approved participants use it.

layout.contents: Heading 'Volunteer tasks' with a short line saying you accept pickups when you are available.
A single on/off toggle labelled 'Available for pickups' with its current state shown in words (Available / Not available).
A capacity field labelled 'Carrying capacity' with a save button. Shows the current saved value.
Cards for claimed donations that need a transporter, each with the donor, receiving NGO, food description, portions, pickup-by time and an 'Accept pickup' button.
Cards for pickups this volunteer has already accepted, each with its status and an 'Open' button.

shows.details: One toggle showing whether the volunteer is currently available.
The volunteer's saved carrying capacity, shown next to its edit field.
Claimed donations awaiting a transporter: food description, portions, pickup-by time, donor name, receiving NGO name, ordered by soonest pickup-by time.
Pickups this volunteer has accepted: food description, portions, pickup-by time, donor, receiving NGO and current status.

actions.action: Turn availability on or off
actions.result: The availability status updates and the volunteer's availability is saved.

actions.action: Set carrying capacity and save
actions.result: The new carrying capacity is saved and shown on the screen.

actions.action: Accept a pickup
actions.result: The pickup moves to accepted pickups under this volunteer; the volunteer is taken to Active Delivery for that pickup.

links.label: Accept pickup
links.when: After a pickup is accepted, to confirm collection and handover.

states.empty: No pickups available: 'No pickups need a transporter right now.' Accepted list shows 'You have not accepted any pickups yet.'
states.loading: Skeleton placeholders for the toggle, capacity field and pickup cards.
states.error: A message saying availability, capacity or the pickup could not be saved, with a retry button; the previous value stays shown.

detail.notes: Carrying capacity unit is not specified in the requirements; use one consistent unit and state it next to the field. Only approved participants can sign in here (admin approval applies). No live GPS or continuous location tracking: do not show a live map or tracked position. Server-side enforcement of status transitions: a pickup already accepted cannot be accepted by another volunteer.

/volunteer-tasks.basis: ["Volunteer Tasks","Where a volunteer toggles availability, sets carrying capacity and accepts pickups.",["Volunteer / NGO Transporter"],[["Volunteer / NGO Transporter","toggle availability, set carrying capacity and accept pickups"]]]

detail.purpose: Where an admin approves or suspends participants, watches active rescues and resolves failed assignments. Used by the Admin persona to keep the pilot network running.

layout.contents: Heading 'Admin Operations' with a one-line description of approving participants, monitoring rescues and resolving failed assignments.
List of pending and existing participants (donors, NGOs, volunteers, sponsors) showing name, role, status and an 'Approve' or 'Suspend' button per row.
List of in-progress rescues showing donation, claiming NGO, volunteer, current status and time since last status update.
List of assignments that failed (for example unaccepted or unconfirmed pickups) with the reason and resolve actions.

shows.details: Name, role, account status (pending, approved, suspended), grouped by status with pending first.
Donation, claiming NGO, assigned volunteer, current status, grouped by rescue with counts for active rescues.
Donation, assignment, failure reason, time of failure, listed for resolution.

actions.action: Approve a pending participant
actions.result: Participant status changes to approved and they can sign in and use their role's screens.

actions.action: Suspend a participant
actions.result: Participant status changes to suspended and they can no longer sign in or act.

actions.action: Monitor active rescues
actions.result: Admin views current status of each rescue in progress without changing it.

actions.action: Resolve a failed assignment
actions.result: Failed assignment is resolved and its donation returns to a state where it can be reassigned or closed.

links.label: Donation ID
links.when: Admin opens a rescue or failed assignment to see its full details and status history.

states.empty: No pending participants, active rescues or failed assignments; each panel shows a short 'Nothing to review' message.
states.loading: Panels show skeleton rows while participants, rescues and failures load.
states.error: A failed load shows an error message with a retry button in the affected panel.

detail.notes: Only the Admin persona may approve, suspend or resolve. Status transitions are enforced on the server. Participants are synthetic in the hackathon pilot.

/admin-operations.basis: ["Admin Operations","Where an admin approves or suspends participants, monitors active rescues and resolves failed assignments.",["Admin"],[["Admin","approve or suspend participants, monitor active rescues and resolve failed assignments"]]]

detail.purpose: Where a volunteer or NGO transporter confirms that they have collected a claimed donation and handed it over to the receiving NGO, and sees the pickup's simple status updates. Used during the pickup itself, after the volunteer has accepted it on Volunteer Tasks.

layout.contents: Heading 'Active delivery' and a one-line note that collection and handover are confirmed here; a link back to Volunteer Tasks.
The accepted pickup: donation food description, portions, pickup-by time, donor restaurant name, receiving NGO name, and a 'View donation' link.
A simple list of status updates for this pickup, newest first, each with status name and time. Shows the current status prominently.
A 'Confirm collection' button with the collected portions shown, and a note that the donation is collected once confirmed.
A 'Confirm handover' button, enabled only after collection is confirmed, with a note that handover passes the food to the receiving NGO.

shows.details: Food description, portions, pickup-by time, donor restaurant, receiving NGO, current status.
Simple list of status changes for this pickup, newest first, with time.
Claimed portions for this pickup, matching the carrying capacity the volunteer indicated.

actions.action: Confirm collection of the food from the donor
actions.result: The pickup status moves to collected and the collection step is locked; handover becomes available.

actions.action: Confirm handover of the food to the receiving NGO
actions.result: The pickup status moves to handed over; the NGO is then asked to confirm the received quantity on its Receipt screen.

actions.action: Open the donation's full details
actions.result: Opens the donation detail screen.

links.label: Back to tasks
links.when: After handover, or when the volunteer wants to return to availability and pickups.

links.label: View donation
links.when: When the volunteer wants to check the donation's handling declarations or status history before collecting.

states.empty: No accepted pickup: a short message saying there is no active delivery, with a link to Volunteer Tasks to accept one.
states.loading: Pickup details and status updates show a loading placeholder until fetched.
states.error: If a confirmation fails, the status does not change, an error message shows, and the volunteer can retry.

detail.notes: No live GPS or location tracking; collection and handover are confirmed by the volunteer's own action only. Status transitions are enforced on the server and cannot be skipped (handover only after collection). Volunteers see only pickups they have accepted. Rescued impact is counted only after the NGO confirms the received quantity, not on handover.

/active-delivery.basis: ["Active Delivery","Where a volunteer confirms collection and handover and sees simple status updates.",["Volunteer / NGO Transporter"],[["Volunteer / NGO Transporter","confirm collection and handover and see status updates"]]]

detail.purpose: Where a CSR sponsor sees campaign recognition and a transparent dashboard of confirmed rescue impact, with its assumptions labelled. Only NGO-confirmed deliveries count toward the figures.

layout.contents: Heading 'Sponsor Impact' and a line saying the figures count only NGO-confirmed deliveries.
The sponsor's campaign recognition, shown as read-only content.
Three cards: confirmed portions delivered, estimated waste avoided (kg), and illustrative costs. Each card is labelled as derived from confirmed data.
Labelled assumptions: waste avoided = portions × 0.35 kg per portion (configurable, disclosed here); illustrative costs are not actual payments; no tax or legal-benefit claim is made.

shows.details: The sponsor's campaign recognition content, read-only.
Total portions from NGO-confirmed receipts only; a single total figure.
Kilograms, calculated as confirmed portions × 0.35 kg; the 0.35 kg factor is shown beside it.
Figures labelled as illustrative, not billed or paid amounts.
Per-portion factor, that only confirmed deliveries count, and the no-certification and no-tax-claim disclaimers.

actions.action: Reads campaign recognition and the impact dashboard.
actions.result: Nothing changes; the screen shows the current confirmed figures and labelled assumptions.

states.empty: No confirmed deliveries yet: portions, waste avoided and costs show zero, with the assumptions still visible.
states.loading: Shows placeholder cards and a loading indicator while figures are fetched.
states.error: Shows a message that the impact figures could not be loaded, with a retry option.

detail.notes: Read-only screen; no editing, exporting or payment actions. Totals must come from NGO-confirmed receipts only. The 0.35 kg per portion factor is configurable and must be disclosed on the screen. Do not present illustrative costs as payments, billing or tax or legal benefits. Do not state food safety certification.

/sponsor-impact.basis: ["Sponsor Impact","Where a CSR sponsor sees campaign recognition and the transparent impact dashboard, with assumptions labelled.",["CSR Sponsor"],[["CSR Sponsor","see campaign recognition and the impact dashboard with assumptions labelled"]]]
